Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 175: Warming Hands on His Neck

At 5:30 in the evening, the bell signaling the end of the afternoon's activities rang on time.

Li Luo and his group went to the cafeteria together, had a simple dinner, and then returned to their respective classrooms.

It was already past six in the evening.

The cold winter wind howled outside the window. The classroom was frigid because no one had been in it all afternoon, so the heating hadn't been turned on.

Li Luo wrapped the red scarf Ying Chanxi had personally knitted for him around his neck, tucking his hands between the layers to warm them with the heat from his neck.

Yan Zhusheng turned her head and watched his hands, couldn't help but rub her own. "Doesn't that make your neck cold?"

"It does," Li Luo said, "but it'll be fine once my hands are warm. You can try it too."

"I can try it?"

"Of course, aren't your hands on your own body?"

"Oh, then I won't be polite."

Yan Zhusheng nodded, then extended both her hands, slipping them into Li Luo's scarf and pressing them firmly against his warm neck.

The chill from her small hands sent a shiver through Li Luo's entire body. He stared at her, utterly baffled, at a loss for words for a moment.

Li Luo: "...Did you misunderstand what I said?"

"Hm?" Yan Zhusheng blinked. "What did I misunderstand?"

"I meant for you to warm them on your own neck."

"But you told me to try it."

"...Fine, my bad." Li Luo was defeated by her innocent expression and raised his hands in surrender. "Are they warm yet? I'm freezing to death."

"They are now." Yan Zhusheng retracted her hands with a satisfied look, feeling them toasty warm. "You're not mad, are you?"

"What would you do if I were mad?"

"Then I'd let you warm your hands on my neck too."

"I really have you to thank for that..."

Li Luo tightened his scarf and glanced at the time. It was still a few minutes until 6:30.

So he called out to Zhu Yufei, "Tell everyone to get ready. We'll be lining up to go downstairs soon, and we need to bring our chairs."

"OK." Zhu Yufei replied, getting up and walking to the podium to tell everyone to prepare. Those who wanted to bring snacks were reminded to get them ready in advance.

That kid, Zhang Guohuang, even brought a pair of binoculars.

After all, with three grade levels and 48 classes crammed onto the basketball court, if you were unlucky enough to sit in the back, it would probably be very hard to see the stage up front.

Just as the bell for 6:30 was about to ring, Kong Junxiang's figure finally appeared at the classroom door. Teacher Ding was nowhere to be seen.

But judging by his glowing face, he must have had a fulfilling day.

It was a pity Li Luo hadn't been a student at Fuyi High in his past life, so he had no idea if Old Kong had eventually won the beauty's heart and let everyone see what a little Kong would look like.

After Kong Junxiang walked into the classroom, the 6:30 evening bell rang on schedule.

A teacher's orderly voice came over the broadcast, instructing each class to form a line, bring their chairs, and proceed downstairs to the basketball court in an orderly fashion.

The students of Class Eight immediately sprang into action, their faces filled with excitement.

Even in the blowing winter wind, the atmosphere in the school building was heated to a fever pitch.

Li Luo picked up his chair and followed the line downstairs.

On the way, Yan Zhusheng carried her chair with both hands, looking left and right with a face full of curiosity.

Li Luo glanced at her and took the initiative to ask, "Do you want me to carry your chair for you?"

Hearing this, Yan Zhusheng immediately shook her head. "It's fine, I can carry it."

"I can't carry mine," Xu Yinghuan, who was walking in front of Yan Zhusheng, said with a laugh as she turned her head. "Class President, can you carry it for me?"

"Carry your own chair," Li Luo criticized righteously. "How can someone so young not even be able to carry a single chair? Classmate Xu Yinghuan, you need to reflect on yourself. Do you exercise diligently? Do you strive to be a model student who is well-rounded in moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic, and labor education?"

"..." Xu Yinghuan was stunned by his words, then looked speechless. "Class President, you're such a hypocrite. Why didn't you say that when you asked Zhusheng just now?"

"That was just a test I was giving to Classmate Yan Zhusheng," Li Luo spouted nonsense with a straight face. "See, she passed my test perfectly, proving herself to be a healthy, independent, and good young person. But I hadn't even gotten to you yet, and you've already willingly fallen from grace."

Xu Yinghuan: "...?"

Li Luo could talk a dead horse back to life. Xu Yinghuan was rendered speechless and could only roll her eyes in the end.

Shao Heqi, who had witnessed the whole thing from the side, was dumbfounded, thinking to himself, *there's a move like that?*

It couldn't help but remind him of the middle school graduation ceremony a few months ago. If he had known Li Luo's move back then, why would he have bothered carrying Jin Yuting's chair?

However, just as their line reached Houde Road, after Yan Zhusheng had listened to Li Luo's long-winded speech, she suddenly said, "I'm a little tired now, Li Luo. Can you help me carry my chair?"

"Really tired?"

"Yeah."

"Then give it to me." Li Luo reached out and hoisted Yan Zhusheng's chair onto his shoulder. "Let's go." Xu Yinghuan, up ahead, heard the commotion and turned to see the scandalous deed of this dog couple. Her eyes widened as she questioned, "Class President, what's the meaning of this? And you say you're not a hypocrite!"

"This is something you wouldn't understand." Li Luo shook his head with a click of his tongue, enlightening Xu Yinghuan, "This is the organization's reward for Yan Zhusheng after she passed the test. It's what she deserves."

Xu Yinghuan: "...Fine, whatever you say is right."

Soon, everyone arrived at the entrance of the basketball court under the night sky and moonlight in an orderly fashion.

At the north end of the court, a temporary stage had been set up against the wall.

And directly in front of the stage was a huge bonfire that had been built, though it had not yet been lit.

On the four corners surrounding the court, four large incandescent lights were already on, illuminating the students on the court.

The seniors from the second and third years were arranged at both ends of the stage, while the first-year students occupied the best viewing spots directly facing the stage, spreading out in a fan shape, row after row.

Class Eight's position was neither good nor bad, located on the left side of the stage, near the middle of the seating arrangement.

With good eyesight, you could still see the situation on stage clearly.

It took about twenty minutes in total for all the students from the three grades of Fuyi High to be seated.

Everyone craned their necks excitedly, looking around, before their gazes finally converged on the stage and the bonfire in front.

The principal, now holding a microphone, had walked onto the stage. He tested the sound and then said with a smile, "Students, you've been waiting for a long time."

"Today, let's not waste any more time with idle talk. Let's start our first segment directly."

"Come, count down with me."

"Ten, nine, eight..."

The students from the second and third years had clearly experienced this scene before and cooperated by starting the countdown.

The first-year students, a little slower on the uptake, also seemed to realize what was about to happen, and they all began to shout excitedly.

"Seven, six, five, four..."

"Three!"

"Two!"

"One!"

"Light the bonfire!"

As soon as his voice fell, the PE teacher below the stage had already doused the bonfire with flammable oil. Then, he threw a tinder into it, instantly igniting the firewood that had long been prepared inside the bonfire.

At first, it was just a small flame.

But gradually, the flame grew larger and more vigorous. The students in the front row could even clearly feel the wave of heat, which instantly blew away the cold winter wind.

The students' spirits also ignited with the burgeoning bonfire, and the atmosphere of the evening party instantly became excited and festive.

The principal was clearly very happy as well. Music immediately started playing, and he launched into a rendition of "The Long March."

When he sang the line "All three armies are wreathed in smiles," the principal made a grand gesture with his hand, signaling the end.

The students all applauded.

The principal, a former military man, now resumed his cheerful, smiling expression and waved his hand. "I won't take up any more of your time. What's the next performance?"

"Oh, the crosstalk from Class Seven, Year Two, right."

"Come, please welcome them!"

After speaking, the principal walked off the stage.

Two students from Class Seven, Year Two, dressed in red and green long gowns, appeared on stage. Their humorous banter, singing, and storytelling made the students below roar with laughter.

Li Luo watched the scenes unfolding on the stage, feeling increasingly emotional.

*So this is what a good high school is like?*

*I must have gone to a fake high school back then!*

"Li Luo." Yan Zhusheng tugged at Li Luo's scarf.

"Hm?"

"The club president is looking for us." Yan Zhusheng pointed to Niu Qingling, who was standing in the back row, waving at them.

Their performance was scheduled for the second-to-last slot.

The last performance was a school-wide choir singing the school anthem, so it was not wrong to say their act was the grand finale.

Although it was still a while before the second-to-last performance, they needed to head over early to prepare.

"Let's go." Li Luo adjusted the scarf around his neck and stood up.

Yan Zhusheng also got up, and the two of them followed Niu Qingling towards the open area behind the stage.

(End of Chapter)

[Extra · Youyu] (1) First Encounter in the Previous Life

Reigniting the Prime of Youth [Extra · Youyu] (1) First Encounter in the Previous Life

On a certain summer evening.

Jincheng Community.

"Not eating at home tonight?"

"Yeah, I made plans with a friend."

"Xiao Jun?"

"No, an online friend. Also a writer."

"A guy or a girl?"

"A guy."

"Oh." Hearing this answer, Lin Xiuhong waved her hand in disappointment. "Go on, then."

With a bang, the door closed.

Li Luo, who had been out of university for a year, left his home and walked towards the subway entrance on the nearby Qiushan Avenue under the last rays of twilight.

He passed the gate of his old middle school, Yucai Middle School, walked down another street, and glanced at Jiangnan Xiaozhu, which was packed with customers at dinnertime, before walking straight into the subway entrance beside it.

After getting on the subway smoothly, Li Luo took out his phone from his pants pocket, found an empty seat, and sat down, heading towards the terminal station, Qianjiang University.

Opening QQ on his phone, Li Luo looked at the chat history.

Liluo: Are we really meeting up?

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: You're so fussy. We're both in Yinjiang District, you don't need to take a plane to meet up.

Liluo: It's just that I've never met anyone I know online before. What you're saying is making me nervous.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: What's there to be nervous about? My treat, just bring your mouth.

Liluo: What are we eating?

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: There's a pretty good barbecue place near Qianjiang University. Are you close?

Liluo: Pretty close, just three stops by subway.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Then it's a date. Seven in the evening, meet me at the south gate of Qianjiang University.

Liluo: Wait, today???

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: What else? You have plans tonight? What plans could a single dog like you have?

Liluo: Don't be so hurtful...

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: So are you coming or not?

Liluo: Just the two of us?

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: I don't know any other authors in Yinjiang District. Just us. Are you afraid I'll sell you off or something?

Liluo: Fine, I'll be there at seven sharp.

After reviewing the chat history, Li Luo checked the time. It was currently 6:40 PM.

Ten minutes on the subway, then walk from the station to the south gate of Qianjiang University, he would definitely be able to make it before seven.

So he sent the other party a message.

Liluo: I'm on the subway, will be there soon.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Holy crap! So punctual?

Liluo: Didn't you say seven o'clock? You're not going to stand me up, are you?

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Of course not! But I need to get ready for a bit, so wait for me a little!

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: There's a Starbucks next to the south gate. If I'm not there, you can sit there for a while first.

Liluo: Okay, I'll let you know when I'm there.

After sending the message, Li Luo put down his phone, leaned back against the subway seat, and emptied his mind.

Memories from the past year since his graduation from university flooded his mind.

After giving up on becoming a chef, he had impulsively jumped into the world of web novels. For the first half-year, it was safe to say he had run into a brick wall.

For the first two months, he couldn't even cross the threshold for a contract, let alone make any money.

He wasn't even qualified to receive the website's full attendance award.

The turning point came two months after he started.

A brain-holed entertainment novel he had written before had poor data during the new book period, couldn't compete with others, and was eliminated after one round of recommendation. So, he had dropped it.

To his surprise, a comment from "Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao" themselves appeared in his comment section, complaining that it was rare to see a somewhat interesting brain-holed novel, only for it to be dropped after just a few days of reading.

Li Luo brazenly replied to the comment, explaining his situation. Because the data was poor, he couldn't continue writing it.

After all, he didn't want to live off his parents at home forever, not earning money or finding a girlfriend, getting nagged by his mom every day.

That kind of life was truly hard to endure.

He desperately needed a successful book, to at least earn his first ever author's payment.

To his surprise, "Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao" actually replied to him.

And it was a long, detailed reply, pointing out the problems with his book and providing several directions for revision and improvement.

For Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao, who already had two books with ten thousand subscriptions at the time, this reply might have just been a whim.

But it had a huge impact on Li Luo. It was as if it had cleared his meridian channels. Many things he had only half-understood before were suddenly made clear.

So Li Luo, following the template of that brain-holed novel, made some revisions, rewrote the beginning, sent it to his editor, and then started a new book.

This time, the results finally showed improvement.

The new book smoothly passed the first four rounds of recommendations, but ultimately lost in the Sanjiang Recommendation PK, forcing him to release it for sale early.

Even so, he achieved a good result of over 800 first-day subscriptions.

In the first month of furiously writing ten thousand words a day, his earnings reached a full eight thousand!

Unfortunately, also because of the daily ten-thousand-word output, the entire framework of the book collapsed when it reached over four hundred thousand words.

Finally, around half a year into his writing career, he chose to finish it at one million words, truly allowing him to cross the million-word milestone.

He had also earned about fifty thousand yuan in royalties.

This made him very happy. He showed off to his parents, treated them to a good meal, bought Li Guohong a carton of cigarettes, and bought Lin Xiuhong a new outfit.

Life suddenly became much better.

But after this book was finished, he faced the problem of the next new book.

Li Luo still had some lingering fear of flopping, so he mustered his courage and cheekily sent a friend request to Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao.

To his surprise, the other person had been reading the book he wrote all along and accepted his friend request very smoothly.

With the help of Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao, he came up with a golden finger for his new book, sorted out the outline, and made ample preparations before starting the new book a month later.

During the two-month new book period, he successfully passed the Sanjiang Recommendation and received the highest honor for a new book.

The first-day subscriptions were 2,500. Now, in the fifth month of writing, it was also the end of his first year as a writer.

In all of this, Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao's help was indispensable.

What he hadn't expected was that, after chatting more, they discovered they were from the same hometown, both living in Yinjiang District, Yuhang City.

Extremely close.

After knowing each other for over half a year, Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao suggested they meet up. Li Luo hesitated for a moment before agreeing.

After all, he had received such a great favor from the other person. Although they were both men and he couldn't offer himself in return, he should at least say thank you in person.

He had originally wanted to treat them, but considering it was their invitation to meet, treating them wasn't urgent.

He could always treat them back next time.

As he was thinking about these things, the subway announcement sounded in his ear.

"Dear passengers, this train has arrived at the terminal station, Qianjiang University. All passengers, please take your personal belongings with you and exit through the left doors."

"Thank you for riding with us. We wish you a pleasant journey. Goodbye."

Hearing the subway announcement, Li Luo stood up from his seat. When the subway slowly came to a stop and the doors opened, he quickly walked out of the car.

As soon as he stepped out of the subway exit, a wave of heat, still quite intense on a summer night, hit him.

Li Luo tugged at his collar a few times to fan himself, confirmed his direction, and then headed for the south gate of Qianjiang University.

On the way, as he crossed the intersection, Li Luo turned to look at the Shidai Tianjie commercial district at the subway exit.

In his memory, the northern part of Yinjiang District hadn't been so lively in the early years. How much time had passed?

Once the subway was built and Shidai Tianjie was completed, the surrounding housing prices skyrocketed as if on a rocket.

With the supporting facilities centered around Qianjiang University, this area, with Shidai Tianjie at its core, radiated outwards, becoming another new commercial hub in Yinjiang District.

Meanwhile, the old commercial hub near Li Luo's home had declined year by year because the subway line didn't pass through there, and foot traffic had plummeted, its former glory gone.

Thinking about this, Li Luo felt a bit emotional.

Although he was now earning over twenty thousand a month from writing, he didn't know how his next book would do. It could very well flop.

A single book, written for a year or two, would come to an end, earning him two to three hundred thousand yuan. That would only be enough to buy a small bedroom here.

For Li Luo, buying a house before marriage, even with a mortgage, was a real challenge.

With that kind of money, it would be better to live in the present and enjoy life a bit more.

Li Luo crossed the intersection, gradually moving away from Shidai Tianjie. He passed through the road between the east gate of Qianjiang University and the dormitory area, turned a corner, and soon arrived at the south gate.

Liluo: I'm at the south gate. If you're not here yet, I'll go into Starbucks to sit for a bit. It's boiling hot outside.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: OKOK! Give me ten minutes!

Liluo: Okay.

Li Luo glanced at the south gate of Qianjiang University. It was summer vacation, so he didn't see many students coming and going.

The Starbucks next to it wasn't very crowded either, because Qianjiang University was on summer break.

Li Luo pushed the door open and walked in. Thinking that Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao would probably pass by the shop later, he chose a seat by the window and even took a photo of the view outside for the other person.

Liluo: I'm sitting by the window. Just let me know when you're here.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Okay! Soon!

Starbucks didn't have a mandatory purchase policy, so Li Luo just sat there, casually scrolling through his phone.

He first checked his book, glanced at some new comments in the comment section, and then saw that Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao's comment had been pushed to the top by readers.

Many people were there to urge him to update and not to slack off.

Li Luo then clicked on Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao's avatar, entered his homepage, where there were only two books.

One, "Literary Era," was written from 2014 to 2017.

The other, "Daoist Gu Changqing," had been written from 2018 until now. Since it was in the final stages, updates were very slow, and he would often take a day or two off, much to the readers' chagrin.

Unlike Li Luo, who specialized in writing light, populist novels, Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao's writing style was relatively delicate and mature, with a faint literary flavor, yet the prose was occasionally witty and humorous.

He was also a master at writing suggestive scenes.

Correspondingly, the difficulty of writing was also much greater.

Li Luo had also discussed some more advanced techniques and theories of web novels with Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao, but honestly, it was easier said than done.

For example, the issue of endings that Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao had recently mentioned to him, saying that the framework needed to be brought together, and some threads from the early and middle stages had to be systematically resolved and grounded in reality.

At the same time, it had to build towards the final climax, with each thread converging at a single point, erupting brilliantly before the finale.

This stuff left Li Luo completely bewildered. He could understand the general idea, but when it came to thinking about the specific methods, he was completely in the dark.

Not to mention the so-called overall theme of the novel that Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao usually talked about, or a certain climactic scene that had been sketched out countless times in his mind before even starting the book.

Things like an outline that uses a single point to drive the entire plot, and the difference and integration of writing major climaxes versus minor rewards.

These were all things that were very difficult for the current Li Luo to fully comprehend.

With these thoughts in mind, Li Luo propped up his chin and looked out the window at the setting sun, feeling a little nervous.

He's a big-shot author, after all. Should I be more careful with my words later?

Although they were already quite familiar online and often joked around while chatting.

But offline, it was ultimately a bit different.

Li Luo felt he should adjust his attitude and be mindful of his words later, so as not to offend the other person.

But this nervousness made him want to go to the bathroom.

Li Luo got up and walked to the restroom. After taking care of his business and washing his hands, he felt his phone vibrate a few times in his pocket.

He dried his hands, took out his phone, and walked out while reading the messages.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: I'm about to arrive, get ready to receive me!

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Are you sitting where you were just now? I don't think I can see you from outside.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Where are you? Where are you?

Seeing these messages, Li Luo knew that Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao was already outside Starbucks, so he simply started walking towards the entrance.

He replied to him as he walked.

Liluo: Wait for me outside, I just went to the bathroom, coming out now.

As he said this, Li Luo walked out the main door of Starbucks, but because he was looking down and typing, he happened to bump into a figure.

"Hiss..."

"Ah!"

A girl was knocked off balance by him and had to grab the door frame to keep from falling.

Li Luo was startled and quickly apologized, "Sorry, sorry, I wasn't paying attention. Are you okay?"

"I'm... I'm fine." The girl in front of him seemed to be in a hurry too. She just waved her hand dismissively and walked into Starbucks.

In a fleeting glance, Li Luo caught a glimpse of her delicate face and her plump, graceful figure.

*Wow... so beautiful...*

Li Luo was stunned, and only averted his gaze after she had walked into Starbucks.

The mature, older-sister type. Dressed up so nicely, I wonder which lucky guy gets her.

Thinking this, Li Luo picked up his phone again and scanned his surroundings, trying to find the Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao who matched the image in his mind.

According to his guess, Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao should be a man a bit older than him.

After all, to have written a book like "Literary Era," set in the early 20th century, several years ago, he couldn't possibly be younger than him.

Plus, with all the skillful suggestive writing in the book, he had to be an old hand at it.

With this in mind, Li Luo blindly guessed that Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao was probably a middle-aged man around 35.

Using this as a standard, he scanned the area around the Starbucks entrance, and then found himself completely lost.

Is this guy messing with me?

Did he not even come?

There was no one who matched the target image.

Thinking this, Li Luo looked down at his phone.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Where are you? Did you go out? I just got inside, didn't see you.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Someone even bumped into me, it hurt so much.

Reading this, Li Luo was completely stunned. His mind buzzed, and then he suddenly whipped his head around.

Liluo: Don't tell me you're a girl???

While asking his suspicion on QQ, Li Luo's gaze returned to the girl he had bumped into earlier.

The next second, their eyes met in mid-air.

The girl walked up to Li Luo, a faint smile on her face. She tilted her head and teased, "You really hurt me when you bumped into me just now. How are you going to compensate me?"

Looking at the girl before him, her long hair cascading to her chest with slightly curled ends, a pair of bright eyes on her delicate, mature face smiling at him, Li Luo was momentarily lost.

She was wearing a simple white T-shirt and a pair of black hot pants that revealed a large expanse of fair skin, with a pair of black sneakers on her feet. She looked youthful and beautiful.

Li Luo simply couldn't connect the Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao he knew online with the smiling girl in front of him.

So much so that when he opened his mouth, his words came out a bit haltingly.

"You, you... you are..."

"You're Liluo, right?" The girl giggled and held out her hand. "I'm Zaoshui. You can also call me Xu Youyu. What's your real name?"

"Li Luo." Li Luo still found it hard to accept this reality, his tone strained as he said, "The Luo from Yingluo, with the 'king' radical and a 'ge' from 'tian ge yi fang'."

"Ah, so your pen name is a homophone? Li Luo, Liluo." Xu Youyu nodded in understanding. "'The sparse fence leads to a deep path, the new green on the trees has yet to form shade.' Your pen name is quite nice."

Li Luo had never even heard of this poem... so he could only nod in agreement, then couldn't help but confirm again, "So you're really Zaoshui? Not his sister or something that he asked to come?"

"...You guy, why don't you believe me?" Xu Youyu rolled her eyes, took out her phone, and showed him the chat history. "Isn't this me? Readers all call me Sister Zaoshui, how could it be fake?""They also call others Squid Girl, Sister Jiao, Sister Qing, and what not."

"..." Xu Youyu was stumped by his question, then said helplessly, "You've seen me in person now, what more do you want? Do you need me to verify my gender for you?"

"Uh... that won't be necessary..." Li Luo subconsciously glanced at the magnificent sight on Xu Youyu's chest and felt that it was probably unnecessary.

In any case, a big-shot author earning tens of thousands or even hundreds of thousands a month wouldn't go to the trouble of posing as a woman just to prank him.

But...

Li Luo looked at Xu Youyu's face, then subconsciously avoided her gaze, his words becoming a bit clumsy.

"Then, then... now... we..."

"Let's go get barbecue." Xu Youyu walked straight outside and waved to him with a smile. "There's a very authentic barbecue place nearby. I'll take you to try it."

Li Luo ate barbecue often too.

His good friend, Zhao Rongjun, had found a good job in Yuhang City after graduation. On weekends, he would meet up with Li Luo for some skewers and beer, enjoying a brief moment of freedom.

But eating barbecue alone with a girl, in his memory, he hadn't had such an experience since high school.

As Xu Youyu led him along the road next to Qianjiang University, Li Luo subconsciously turned to glance at her side profile, his eyes hazy for a moment.

He almost thought he was dreaming.

How could he dare to dream that the big-shot author who taught him to write web novels was a beautiful girl?

But at this moment, such an absurd scene was playing out in reality.

Xu Youyu obviously couldn't understand Li Luo's current mood.

As she walked, she explained to him, "This barbecue place isn't really a restaurant. It's more like a gathering place for barbecue enthusiasts."

"My dad has a teacher who loves barbecue. After retiring, he had nothing to do, so he started messing with barbecue."

"But eating alone wasn't satisfying, so he would invite a few friends, and sometimes some students he used to teach from nearby, to have some barbecue."

"Because the taste was so good, word spread, and it became known in some small circles at Qianjiang University."

"Usually, outsiders can't get a taste even if they want to. I had to ask my dad to save me a spot so I could bring you here today."

As she spoke, Xu Youyu led him through several twists and turns into a small alley, where they found the barbecue place.

"Good evening, Granny Yu." As soon as Xu Youyu entered, she greeted an old woman who was tidying up tables and chairs.

"Oh, it's Little Xu's girl." Granny Yu looked at Xu Youyu, her face breaking into a smile. "Come, come, sit here. Your dad told me to save you a spot."

After seating Xu Youyu and Li Luo, Granny Yu looked them over without saying much, just smiling as she placed a piece of paper on the table and handed them a pen. "Same old rules, write it down yourselves."

"Got it." Xu Youyu took the paper and pen and looked at Li Luo. "Anything you don't eat?"

Li Luo shook his head.

So Xu Youyu wrote vigorously on the paper. After finishing, she handed it to Li Luo for a look. "Anything else you want to eat, just write it down."

Li Luo looked at the already filled paper and shook his head repeatedly. "That's too much, it's definitely enough."

"Then let's go with this for now." Xu Youyu stood up and gave the menu to Granny Yu, then went straight to the refrigerator, pulled out a whole case of beer, placed it by the table, and asked with a grin, "Liluo, you can drink, right? Don't tell me you can't."

"Sister Zaoshui drinks?" Li Luo asked, surprised.

"Drinking helps with inspiration." Xu Youyu raised an eyebrow at him, took out two bottles of beer, skillfully opened them, and handed one to Li Luo. "How about a toast to start?"

Since the girl had said so, Li Luo naturally wouldn't be shy. He clinked bottles with Xu Youyu.

This experience was truly strange... He had never seen a girl drink so boldly.

Watching Xu Youyu chug down half a bottle of beer, Li Luo started to doubt again whether she was a man in disguise.

The two of them chatted casually while drinking. Soon, the barbecue they had ordered was brought to the table one after another.

Li Luo took a bite, and his eyes lit up. He found that the taste was really different from the barbecue places outside.

"Here in Yuhang City, many barbecue places claim to serve lamb skewers, but many of them actually use duck meat," Xu Youyu said with a smile. "Especially those that only do takeout, it's very hard to find authentic ones."

"Hmm... now that you mention it." Li Luo took another lamb skewer and found that the texture was indeed different from the ones he usually ate. "I think you're right."

"By the way." Xu Youyu picked up her beer bottle, clinked it with his again, and after swallowing the beer, she continued, "How old are you? You look a bit young."

"Born in '99, why?"

"Huh? A year younger than me." Xu Youyu smiled. "So you're a little brother. Call me 'big sister' and let me hear it."

"Didn't I already call you Sister Zaoshui?" Li Luo said helplessly.

However, he hadn't expected Xu Youyu to be a year older than him.

Of course, based on common sense, it would be logical for Li Luo to assume Xu Youyu was in her thirties, given that Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao had been writing for so many years.

But looking at her delicate and youthful face, he really couldn't associate it with the age of thirty.

He would have believed it if someone said she was even younger than him.

Being a year older than him was an age that seemed to match her appearance.

But...

"So when did you start writing?" Li Luo asked curiously.

"During the summer vacation of my first year of high school, I think," Xu Youyu said with a smile. "My first book then was 'Literary Era'."

"You wrote that in high school?" Li Luo fell silent.

Suddenly, he felt that the gap between people was just so vast.

What was he doing in high school?

Either slacking off in class or playing games at the internet cafe on weekends.

"It was a hobby in high school, and it also helped me earn some pocket money," Xu Youyu nodded and continued, "Then when I went to university, I felt I could do this long-term, so I continued writing seriously."

"Then back then," Li Luo suddenly asked curiously, "how did you find my brain-holed entertainment novel?"

"I was quite surprised at the time, since it was a new book with only about a hundred thousand words."

"I never expected a big-shot author like you would be reading it and even leave a comment."

"Oh, that." Xu Youyu frowned, trying hard to recall. "I remember it was someone, can't quite remember who."

"Anyway, I saw it on my Moments. It was probably a younger schoolmate, she posted a recommendation for the book."

"I found it strange at the time because this schoolmate rarely posts on her Moments, so I was surprised she would read web novels and even recommend one."

"So out of curiosity, I went to check it out, found it quite interesting, and left a supportive comment for you."

Hearing Xu Youyu's explanation, Li Luo fell into deep thought.

Was his luck that good?

"The younger schoolmate you mentioned is?"

"I can't remember, it was so long ago," Xu Youyu shook her head. "It probably wasn't someone I knew well, otherwise I would have just messaged her directly."

Since she said that, Li Luo didn't press further.

He just chalked it up to good luck, that his book happened to be seen by a female reader at the right time.

He had to admit, it was a kind of fate.

They ate barbecue for over two hours.

At the beginning, their conversation wasn't very deep. They just got a general understanding of each other's situations, then chatted about topics related to web novels.

Chatting in a field they were both familiar with was a very comfortable thing.

And extending from web novels, since they both started out writing entertainment-themed novels, they naturally talked about the entertainment industry, and the film and music works of recent years.

It had to be said that for them to have known each other for over half a year and successfully met up, their personal tastes had many similarities.

After a long chat and finishing over ten bottles of beer, Xu Youyu got up to pay the bill, and she and Li Luo walked out of the barbecue place.

In the warm summer night breeze, as they walked through the small alley, Li Luo turned to look at the girl reeking of alcohol, his mind a little dazed again.

"Liluo."

"Hm?"

"We're friends now, right?"

"Of course."

"Then let's take a picture."

"Huh?"

"What 'huh'? Come here."

Xu Youyu raised her phone, aimed it at the two of them, and took a photo together.

"Alright, it's getting late. Let's go our separate ways."

"Okay." Li Luo nodded, but looking at her reeking of alcohol, he couldn't help but ask, "Are you sure you'll be okay going back like this? Do you want me to walk you?"

"Are you sure you want to walk me?" Xu Youyu tilted her head and looked at him with a grin. "My home is right inside this community, and my parents are waiting for me. Do you want me to invite you up for a bit?"

"Uh... that won't be necessary." Li Luo quickly waved his hands. "It's just that when we were chatting online, you said you lived alone."

"Oh, I usually rent a place outside," Xu Youyu nodded. "But I don't live near here."

"I brought you here for barbecue today, so I'm just stopping by home on the way."

"No wonder." Li Luo nodded in realization, then said, "Then I'll just walk you to the community gate, and then I'll head home."

"Okay, thanks."

After escorting Xu Youyu to the entrance of the nearby community, Li Luo watched her slightly swaying figure, took a deep breath, and slowly exhaled.

He only turned to leave after her back disappeared around the corner. After getting on the subway home, he even slapped his own face.

Looking at his reflection in the subway window, Li Luo felt like he was in a dream.

To think that Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao was actually a girl... and so young, only a year older than him.

Li Luo scratched his head. His slightly inflated ego, from his new book reaching four thousand average subscriptions, instantly calmed down.

There are always people better than you, and heavens beyond heavens.

On the other side, Xu Youyu returned home. As soon as she pushed the door open and walked in, before she could even change her shoes, she saw her parents sitting solemnly on the living room sofa.

Hearing the noise at the entrance, the two of them turned their heads in unison to look at their daughter in the entryway.

"You're back?" Cui Suling looked at her daughter, patted the empty spot on the sofa next to her, and said, "Come, sit."

"Why are you guys so serious?" Xu Youyu changed into her slippers with a smile, walked over to her mom, and sat down, throwing an arm around Cui Suling's neck. "Mom, a kiss."

"Go away, go away! You reek of alcohol!" Cui Suling pushed her away with a look of disgust. "Why did you drink? Didn't you say you were just treating a friend to barbecue?"

"Yeah, how can you eat barbecue without drinking?"

"I heard it was a guy?" Cui Suling narrowed her eyes and asked.

"What's wrong?" Xu Youyu tilted her head and asked, "Weren't you guys the ones who told me not to always stay cooped up in my rented apartment and to go out and socialize more?"

"So where did this guy come from?" Cui Suling asked. "I've never seen you with any guy friends."

"We met online."

"An online friend?!" Cui Suling's voice went up an octave. "Why didn't you say so earlier? Are online friends people you can just meet casually?"

"It's not as dramatic as you think," Xu Youyu said, exasperated. "He's a writer like me."

At these words, Xu Rongsheng, who had been silent all this time, finally spoke up, "A writer?"

"Yeah."

"Where's he from?"

"A local."

"What's his family situation?"

"...How would I know that?" Xu Youyu didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "Why would I ask someone that for no reason? It's not like I'm on a blind date, I'm just making a friend."

"You're not dating?" Cui Suling asked in surprise.

"At least not yet, right?" Xu Youyu blinked and teased with a smile, "But he seems like a nice person. Mom, if you're in a hurry, I could give it a try?"

"I didn't say that." Cui Suling quickly shook her head. "He's a writer, does he make money? From what you usually say, your line of work is pretty unstable, right?"

"That's true." Xu Rongsheng nodded. "I've looked into it. Youyu's current results are already quite impressive on their website. What are this guy's results?"

"Uh... a little bit worse than mine?"

"How much is a little bit?"

"Probably less than half of mine?"

"How is that a little bit?" Cui Suling was speechless. "You should be careful."

"I told you we're just friends. It was you guys who were interrogating me like this." Xu Youyu sighed. "Anyway, it's not a big deal. If you two have nothing else, I'm going to bed."

Watching their daughter stand up and walk into the bedroom, the couple on the sofa exchanged a look.

After Xu Youyu left, they started whispering.

"What's the situation, you should ask Auntie Yu more about it."

"Didn't I ask? She just went to the shop with a guy, had some barbecue, and seemed to have a good time," Xu Rongsheng frowned. "Weren't you the one rushing her to get married? Now that she's started looking, you're not happy?"

"But she should find someone of equal social standing, right?"

"We don't know the other person's situation yet, do we?" Xu Rongsheng shook his head. "I think you should meddle less. The more you push, the more rebellious she'll get."

"But if I don't push, she won't look at all." Cui Suling looked helpless. "You said not to push, but she didn't date at all during her four years of university. Now she's been graduated for two years and is about to turn thirty, how can I not be anxious?"

"Alright, alright, at least she's willing to go out on dates now." Xu Rongsheng's ears were getting tired of it too. He stood up and patted his pants. "If you're so anxious, just have her invite the guy over for dinner next time."

Jincheng Community.

Li Luo returned home.

Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong had already gone to bed early, as they had to work at their breakfast stall the next morning.

He took a shower in the bathroom, and after lying down in his bedroom, he checked his phone.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: (Image)

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: The photo is a bit ugly, I don't usually edit my pictures, so just make do.

Liluo: It's great, the green leaf sets off the beautiful flower.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: How many girls have you deceived with that smooth tongue of yours?

Liluo: Haven't managed to deceive even one yet.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: For some reason, I don't believe you.

Liluo: I've never even been in a relationship, what's there to lie to you about?

Liluo: You treated me to dinner this time, let me treat you next time. I also have to thank you for always teaching me how to write web novels.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Haha okay, I won't be polite then.

The two chatted for a long time, from past ten in the evening until midnight.

Finally.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: I'm going to sleep now, can't stay up any longer. Good night.

Liluo: OK, good night.

Saying good night, but in fact, after saying good night, many people wouldn't sleep at all.

Li Luo tossed and turned in bed in the middle of the night, unable to fall asleep.

Finally, he got up from bed, turned on his computer, entered the author's assistant, and intended to write for a while.

But just after he started writing, he saw that in a word count competition room that Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao had pulled him into yesterday, the word count of someone with the ID "Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao" was also slowly increasing.

The other person obviously noticed this too.

The QQ icon in the bottom right corner of his computer screen started flashing.

Zaoshui Hui Zhanggao: Hey, you said good night and then secretly started grinding?

Liluo: Weren't you the one who said good night first? Turns out you were planning to secretly grind behind my back, huh?

Reading the message from the other person, both of them, in their respective bedrooms, couldn't help but chuckle.

(End of Chapter)
